title: 1986 AHSME Problem 30
statement: The number of real solutions \((x,y,z,w)\) of the simultaneous equations \[ \begin{aligned} 2y&=x+\frac{17}{x},\\ 2z&=y+\frac{17}{y},\\ 2w&=z+\frac{17}{z},\\ 2x&=w+\frac{17}{w}. \end{aligned} \] is

solutions.text:
Each expression \(t+\frac{17}{t}\) has the same sign as \(t,\) so all four variables have the same sign. Suppose first that they are positive. By AM-GM, every variable is at least \(\sqrt{17}.\) For \(t\gt\sqrt{17},\) \[ \frac{t+\frac{17}{t}}{2}\lt t. \] If any variable exceeded \(\sqrt{17},\) the equations would give the impossible strict cycle \(x\gt y\gt z\gt w\gt x.\) Hence the only positive solution is \[ x=y=z=w=\sqrt{17}. \] Negating all four variables preserves the system, giving exactly one negative solution, with all variables equal to \(-\sqrt{17}.\) Thus there are two real solutions.

Therefore the correct answer is B.
hints: The equations force all four variables to have the same sign
For positive \(t,\) study \(f(t)=\frac{t+\frac{17}{t}}{2}\) relative to \(\sqrt{17}\) and to \(t\)
